Service

SaaS product design that drives growth.

I design intuitive, scalable SaaS products through deep user research, strategic information architecture, and tight collaboration with engineering — from the first wireframe to the last component spec.

B2B

Ship

Dev-ready handoff

Capabilities

What's included.

User Research

Interviews, usability testing, and analytics review to understand how users actually work — not how we think they work. Research that leads to decisions, not decks.

Information Architecture

Logical structure and navigation flow built around user mental models and task frequency. Role-based IA for multi-tenant platforms with different user types.

Interaction Design

Micro-interactions, workflow patterns, and progressive disclosure that make complex functionality feel intuitive and reduce cognitive load on repeat tasks.

Design Systems

Scalable component libraries with token architecture, consistent interaction patterns, and documentation that design and engineering both actually use.

Prototyping

Interactive prototypes for testing and stakeholder alignment — from low-fidelity concept through high-fidelity specification, matched to what each stage needs.

Developer Handoff

Detailed specifications, component documentation, and continued support through implementation. Design does not end at Figma export.

Process

How I approach a SaaS design engagement.

01

Research & Strategy

Stakeholder interviews, user research, and analytics review to build a shared picture of what users need and where the product is currently failing them.

02

UX Architecture

Design the core information architecture and workflow patterns. The structural work that determines whether the product makes sense — before any visual design.

03

UI Design & Systems

High-fidelity interfaces built within or alongside a design system. Consistency enforced through components, not manual review.

04

Testing & Iteration

Usability testing against real tasks with real users. Findings fed directly back into design — not filed and forgotten.
